cards.title: My son is leaving home for university
cards.body: A parent grapples with empty nest syndrome as their eldest heads off to university with new saucepans in tow. While 'empty nesting' is natural, the emotional reality has knocked them for six.

cards.title: I've forgotten so much about baby care
cards.body: A second-time parent is surprised by how much they've forgotten about infant basics like feeding, teething, and digestion. Their mum's practical help has stirred up memories of their own carefree childhood.

cards.title: Should we let AI do parenting for us?
cards.body: Tech companies offer eye-movement trackers and 'optimized nap predictions' to parents. But do families actually need these tools, or are they solutions to problems that don't exist?

cards.title: 5 things to know about breastfeeding
cards.body: Breastfeeding research is constantly evolving with new findings. Here are five evidence-based insights every new and expecting parent should know.

cards.title: Could your child's anxiety actually be strep?
cards.body: A strep infection can transform a calm child into an anxious one almost overnight, yet few parents check for it. Understanding this connection could help identify the real cause of childhood anxiety.

cards.title: Vaping is addictive—how to help youth quit
cards.body: Vaping addiction is harder to break than many realize, affecting young people across communities. Families, schools, and support networks play crucial roles in recovery and prevention.

cards.title: Emotional regulation is key harm prevention
cards.body: Teaching children to tolerate difficult feelings is more than just a soft skill—it's crucial prevention. Learning emotional regulation can help prevent aggression, addiction, and violence in young people.

cards.title: Parent faces prison for negligence in shooting
cards.body: A Georgia father's sentencing reinforces a growing legal precedent: parents can face criminal responsibility when negligence contributes to a minor committing mass violence. This case sets important legal expectations for parental accountability.

cards.title: ADHD skepticism has real consequences
cards.body: ADHD skepticism isn't harmless—it has serious consequences, especially for those already unlikely to have their struggles recognized. Children and teens are paying the price when their difficulties are dismissed.

cards.title: Understanding autism spectrum: ongoing debate
cards.body: There's a continuing row over whether defining such a broad spectrum as autism actually helps families. Experts disagree on how to best support and understand neurodivergent children.
